points.description: Gives steady-state θss = 0.800 (from θss = b·Nff/(c+b·k1) = 0.75×8/(6+0.75×2) = 6/7.5, using Nff=8, k1=2) and the resulting tracking error of 20% below the reference (−20%). Accept error stated as 20% undershoot/shortfall; the magnitude must be 20%.

Explains that Nff is a feedforward gain on the reference path, outside the feedback loop, so feedback (k1, k2 on measured state, no integrator/no error-driven correction) cannot correct the DC gain error, and the actuator gain error appears directly in the steady-state output. Merely restating that the output is low, without reference to Nff being outside the feedback path / uncorrected by feedback, earns no mark.

rubric.notes: Full marks need θss = 0.800 with a −20% (20% shortfall) error, and a correct explanation that Nff is outside the feedback loop so it is not corrected. Each point is worth 1 mark, all or nothing. A wrong θss from an earlier slip loses only the first point.
rubric.answer_key: Nominal gains from part (a): Nff = 8, k1 = 2 (nominal DC gain b·Nff/(c+b·k1) = 8/8 = 1). At steady state θ̈=θ̇=0, so cθ = b(Nff r − k1θ), giving θss = b·Nff·r/(c + b·k1). With b = 0.75: θss = 0.75×8/(6+0.75×2) = 6/7.5 = 0.800. Tracking error = (0.8−1)/1 = −20% (20% undershoot). Reason: Nff is a feedforward gain on the reference path outside the feedback loop; the state feedback has no integrator or error signal to correct DC calibration error, so the actuator gain error passes directly into the steady-state gain.
